[Neutral · RONI -0.4 °C]{.archive-roni-badge}

December-February 2014 Relative Oceanic Niño Index: a three-month measure of tropical Pacific sea-surface temperature anomalies relative to the tropics. [NOAA CPC data](https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/analysis_monitoring/enso/roni/).
:::

Cool-season maps cover October 1-March 31. Precipitation ranks use water years 1982-2025; temperature departures use 1991-2020 normals. The full water year ends September 30 and includes months outside the cool season. These maps do not attribute local conditions solely to ENSO.

## Snow season

October-May SNODAS model estimates. Peak SWE is the highest daily 
snow-water equivalent; snow-covered days count dates with at least 
0.1 inch SWE. Source gaps or screened cells may leave blank areas.

::: {.dashboard-map-grid}
::: {.dashboard-map-card}
![Peak snow water equivalent](../../maps/generated/snodas/seasonal-archive/wy2014/peak_swe.png)

::: {.archive-map-description}
Maximum daily SWE during October-May, in inches.
:::

::: {.dashboard-card-actions}
[Open full-resolution PNG](../../maps/generated/snodas/seasonal-archive/wy2014/peak_swe.png){.btn .btn-sm .btn-outline-primary}

![Snow-covered days](../../maps/generated/snodas/seasonal-archive/wy2014/snow_days.png)

:::

::: {.dashboard-map-card}
![Peak SWE departure from median](../../maps/generated/snodas/seasonal-archive/wy2014/peak_swe_departure.png)

::: {.archive-map-description}
Seasonal peak SWE minus the WY2005-WY2025 median seasonal peak, in inches. White marks departures within +/-1 inch where median peak SWE is at least 1 inch. Gray marks typically little snow (median peak below 1 inch) with departure within +/-1 inch; larger departures retain brown/blue colors. Beige marks unavailable data or reference support.
:::

::: {.dashboard-card-actions}
[Open full-resolution PNG](../../maps/generated/snodas/seasonal-archive/wy2014/peak_swe_departure.png){.btn .btn-sm .btn-outline-primary}
:::
:::

::: {.dashboard-map-card}
![Peak SWE percent of median](../../maps/generated/snodas/seasonal-archive/wy2014/peak_swe_percent_median.png)

::: {.archive-map-description}
Seasonal peak SWE divided by the WY2005-WY2025 median seasonal peak, times 100. Percentages require a median of at least 1 inch; gray marks lower medians and beige marks unavailable data or support. This is a ratio, not a percentile.
:::

::: {.dashboard-card-actions}
[Open full-resolution PNG](../../maps/generated/snodas/seasonal-archive/wy2014/peak_swe_percent_median.png){.btn .btn-sm .btn-outline-primary}
:::
:::

:::

Companions compare one screened October-May peak per year, including the displayed year in the reference. Peak dates can differ among years and pixels; these are not same-date comparisons. At least 18 eligible reference years and 95% daily coverage per eligible year are required. Existing documented peak masks and archive review cautions are retained.
